spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The residue evaluation pays off by turning every alternating zeta summand into the same integral family; moving the n-sum inside then collapses the entire discrete dependence to the single csc(pi x^2) kernel. The compression from infinitely many rational terms to one explicit kernel is the operative step.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source evaluates the x^4+n^2 integral by residues, substitutes it into the alternating representation of zeta(1/2+ib), interchanges summation and integration, and applies a closed formula for the alternating sum over 1/(x^4+n^2). This yields Eq. (2.6), an integral involving x^{-2ib} and 1-pi x^2 csc(pi x^2).
directed.conceptual_reading: A termwise residue representation becomes useful only because all terms share an x-variable and a summable rational dependence on n. The summation identity eliminates the discrete index and exposes a hyperbolic or trigonometric kernel whose dependence on the spectral parameter is isolated in a power of x.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Two bridge objects are composed: the residue integral converts n^{-ib}/sqrt(n) into a rational n-kernel, and the alternating rational-series identity converts that kernel into csc(pi x^2). Their composition carries the Dirichlet series to a single integral representation.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The source asserts, but does not analyze, conditions for exchanging the infinite sum and integral. The displayed residue evaluation and summation identity are essential proof burdens, so Eq. (2.6) cannot be treated as established solely from the prose description.
directed.uncertainty: Two-dimensional extraction makes the prefactors, powers, signs, and parentheses in Eqs. (2.3)-(2.6) uncertain. The transformation sequence is well supported, while any formula-exact transcription remains conditional on scan verification.

supported: The span supports the stated chain: evaluate the residue integral, substitute it termwise, interchange sum and integral, apply the alternating rational-series identity, and obtain the csc(pi x^2) integral.
The composition of a residue bridge with a summation-identity bridge is a substantive and source-grounded conceptual reading.
The candidate correctly preserves the unproved interchange and the displayed identities as proof burdens.
inference: Describing the elimination of the discrete index as compression into one explicit kernel is a reasonable interpretation of Eqs. (2.4)-(2.6).
unsupported_or_imported: The directed reading imports a 'hyperbolic' kernel: this span reaches the trigonometric csc(pi x^2) kernel, whereas sinh appears only after a later change of variables.
The claim that spectral-parameter dependence is isolated in a power of x needs an 'inside the integral' qualification, because b also remains in the external prefactors of Eq. (2.6).

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source lists a representation of zeta(s) using exp(-y)/cosh(y), rewrites it with denominator exp(y)+1 for Re(s)>0, and then records a Ramanujan integral using y^{-s}(log(y)-Gamma'(y)/Gamma(y)) for 0<=Re(s)<1. These are said to resemble Eq. (2.8).
directed.conceptual_reading: Placing the formulas side by side makes kernel choice and admissible domain the comparison axes. The first alternative uses a thermal-looking hyperbolic denominator, while the second transfers structure into the logarithmic derivative of Gamma; each exposes different analytic data without being shown to be the same transformation as the new kernel.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The common bridge is an integral transform with a power weight in y, but the payload changes among 1/sinh-type subtraction, cosh or exp(y)+1, and log-Gamma-derivative kernels. This comparison suggests multiple representations of the same function rather than a proved map between them.
directed.boundary_or_failure: No derivation connects Eqs. (2.9)-(2.11) to Eq. (2.8), and resemblance does not imply equivalence, interchangeability, or shared continuation properties. The stated domains differ and must remain attached to their respective formulas.
directed.uncertainty: Powers, Gamma factors, prefactors, and domain inequalities are formula-sensitive in the extracted text. The identities and comparison role are source-grounded, but exact transcription should be checked against the scan.
